newsitem.title: ISRAEL: No Israel-PLO deal on Hebron after six weeks.
newsitem.headline: No Israel-PLO deal on Hebron after six weeks.

text.p: Israeli and Palestinian negotiators on Friday ended their sixth week of talks on the fate of the West Bank town of Hebron without clinching a deal.
"Unfortunately there is still no progress," Palestinian President Yasser Arafat told reporters before inaugurating a housing project in self-ruled Gaza.
Arafat said he hoped a deal clearing the way for Israel to transfer most of Hebron to Palestinian control would soon be clinched but that big differences remained.

Negotiators failed in overnight talks to break an impasse over Israel's demand its troops be allowed to enter PLO-run areas in Hebron -- where 400 Jews live and study amidst 100,000 Arabs -- in "hot pursuit" of suspected guerrillas.
"The Israelis' insistence to have the right to re-enter areas handed over to the Palestinians led to disagreements," PLO negotiator Major General Abdel Razak al-Yahya told Reuters.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu wants to alter the Hebron accord signed by the dovish government he ousted last May to bolster safeguards for Jewish settlers in the volatile town.
Palestinians reject any modifications to the signed deal.

"The Arab view of bargaining with Israel...is collective bargaining. We bargain and they collect. That is no longer the principle," Netanyahu told American Jewish fundraisers in Seattle by satellite from Israel on Friday.
Netanyahu on Wednesday cancelled a U.S. trip to meet the fundraisers in hopes of clinching a Hebron deal.

He said Israel wanted the Palestinian Authority to extradite "terrorists" from self-rule areas to Israel, to disarm militant Islamic groups, and to cease "hostile propaganda" against the Jewish state.

"When I raise all these things it irritates people...I'd rather fall back on (late Israeli Prime Minister) Golda Meir who said 'I'd rather be irritating and alive than pleasant and dead'," he told the fundraisers.
Israeli government spokesman Moshe Fogel acknowledged talks remained snagged: "There is no change." The sides were due to return to the bargaining table on Sunday.

Tensions ran high in Hebron on Friday. Israeli and Palestinian sources said shots were heard near an army post outside a heavily fortified Jewish enclave in the city centre. There were no injuries or damage. The army said it was checking the report. Witnesses said Israeli soldiers dashed through a crowded Arab market towards the area of the reported shooting.
A Jewish settler leader demonstrating with some 50 other protesters outside Netanyahu's office against a future Hebron redeployment quickly responded to the incident.

"This perhaps illustrates what can happen again and again when the Palestinian Authority will be there and (someone) opens fire...How will the Israeli army be able to get there to prevent incidents like this?" Aharon Domb told Israel radio.
Fear of bloodshed is one of the few things Hebron's Palestinians share with the Jews in their midst.

U.S.-born Baruch Goldstein, a Jew from adjacent Kiryat Arba settlement, massacred 29 Palestinian worshippers at the traditional burial place of the biblical Abraham in Hebron, a site revered by Jews and Moslems, in February 1994.
